author: TEDx Talks
description:
As AI reshapes how content is created and consumed, the ability to communicate with authenticity and impact has never been more important. In this talk, Louise Beale explores how to speak with clarity, confidence and credibility in a world where voices are amplified, but trust is harder to earn. 

Louise Beale is a broadcast journalist and media professional with extensive experience in television news. Having spent years reporting and communicating under pressure, she now works at the intersection of media, communication, and emerging technology. Louise focuses on how human presence, credibility, and storytelling remain essential skills especially as AI transforms how content is created and consumed. Her TEDx talk explores what television news has taught her about speaking powerfully, authentically, and responsibly in the age of artificial intelligence. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more a
title: How to speak powerfully in the age of AI | Louise Beale | TEDxNorthampton

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Kevser Çimen, bu konuşmasında gönüllülüğü yalnızca yardım etme pratiği olarak değil; toplumsal adalet, birlikte hareket etme ve “işe yararlılık” duygusu üzerinden yeniden düşünmeye davet ediyor.

“Kötülük Gürültülü Değil” başlığı altında Çimen, acil olanla gerçekten ihtiyaç duyulan arasındaki farkı, otoriteye rağmen sorumluluk almanın anlamını ve gönüllülüğün bazen “feleğin çarkına çomak sokmak” olduğunu anlatıyor. Güven kavramının erozyona uğradığı, küresel krizlerin bireyleri ve toplumları edilgenliğe sürüklediği bir çağda; samimiyetin, birlikte hareket etmenin ve değer temelli aktivizmin önemine dikkat çekiyor.

Bu konuşma, izleyiciyi şu sorularla baş başa bırakıyor: İyilik gerçekten gürültülü olmak zorunda mı? Toplumsal adalet için harekete geçmek, bazen en sessiz ama en etkili direniş biçimi olabilir mi?
.......
In this talk, Kevser Çimen invites the audience to rethink volunteering not merely as an act of helping, but as a practice rooted in social justice, collective action, an
title: Evil Is Not Loud  / Kötülük Gürültülü Değil | Kevser Çimenli | TEDxAlsancak Salon

description:
**Türkçe Konuşma Özeti**

Kaan Bayhan, bu konuşmasında gürültü çağında öz-yönetim, kariyer inşası ve farkındalık arasındaki ilişkiyi ele alıyor. Dış dünyanın hız, beklenti ve dikkat dağıtıcı unsurlarla çoğaldığı bir dönemde, insanın kendi özbilgisini duyabilme kapasitesinin güçlü bir içsel kas hâline gelmesi gerektiğini vurguluyor.

Alışkanlıkların, yaşamımızı çoğu zaman fark etmeden yöneten sessiz sistemler olduğunu belirten Bayhan; bu sistemleri tanımanın, gerektiğinde dönüştürmenin ya da durdurmanın kişisel liderlik için kritik olduğunu anlatıyor. Konuşma, farkında olmanın yalnızca içsel bir pratik değil; kariyer kararlarında, değişimle ilişkimizde ve liderlikte ritim kurabilme becerisinde dönüştürücü bir güç olduğunu ortaya koyuyor.

Kaan Bayhan, izleyiciyi şu sorularla baş başa bırakıyor: Gürültüye rağmen kendimizi nasıl duyabiliriz? Alışkanlıklarımızı bizi yöneten görünmez mekanizmalar olmaktan çıkarıp bilinçli bir gelişim aracına nasıl dönüştürebiliriz?
.........

Geçmişten bugüne, bugünden geleceğe uzanan bu yolculukta semboller yalnızca işaretler değildir; insanın kendini, dünyayı ve hakikati anlamlandırma biçimidir. Efe Elmas, izleyiciyi kavramlar ve anlamlar arasında dolaştırırken, daha anlaşılabilir bir yaşam için sembollerin dilini yeniden okumaya davet ediyor.
.....
Just as the ego searches for the Self, human beings search for wholeness, meaning, and the native language of the world throughout life. In this talk, Efe Elmas explores how symbols, concepts, and meanings shape our everyday experience through a semiotic perspective.

Moving between the past and the future, this journey reveals that symbols are not merely signs; they are ways of understanding ourselves, the world, and tr
title: The Language of Symbols  / Sembollerin Dili  | Efe Elmas | TEDxAlsancak Salon

description:

Türk kültürünü dünyaya tanıtan, Anadolu kadın başlıkları ve geleneksel giyim kültürü üzerine yaptığı çalışmalarla kültürel mirasın görünürlüğüne öncülük eden Sabiha Tansuğ’un izinde ilerleyen bu konuşma; bir fincan kahvenin, bir müze fikrinin ve bir kültürel temsil anının nasıl kalıcı bir etkiye dönüşebileceğini sorguluyor. Bugün Sabiha Tansuğ’un mirası, İzmir Bademler Köyü’nde adına kurulan özel müzede de yaşamaya devam ediyor.

Yıldız Gürgün, sektörel turizm deneyimini özel müzecilik, uluslararası kültürel etki ve kültür yönetimi perspektifiyle harmanlayarak izleyiciyi şu sorularla baş başa bırakıyor: Bir kültürel deneyimi güçlü bağlarla inşa etmenin sıradışı yolları nelerdir? Doğru anda gösterilen cesaret, kültürel değerleri görünür kılmaya yeterli olabi

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Cecilia Yip has lived through many moments others might call highlights: award-winning roles, beloved characters, and a new stage at the age of 62. Yet in this talk, she looks beyond the applause and turns toward the part of the journey that is rarely seen.
For many years, Yip struggled with self-doubt. Even after receiving recognition, she found it difficult to accept her own achievements, often feeling that success was accidental or belonged to others. The voice saying “you can do better” became a pressure with no clear end. Through time, reflection, and the courage to try again, she gradually learned to face the imperfect parts of herself and rebuild a gentler relationship with who she is.
For Yip, the other side of a highlight is not darkness, nor is it simply failure. It is the quiet process of making peace with oneself — of no longer hiding from imperfection, and beginning to live with greater openness, courage, and self-acceptance. CECILIA YIP is one of the most celebrated acto
title: What Does It Take to Truly Like Yourself? | Cecilia YIP | TEDxThe Bund Women

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Jing Li has lived through many turning points that others might call rebellious: leaving a secure position at CCTV to start her own business, continuing to host while eight months pregnant, and later turning her attention to a subject many people rarely speak about — menopause.
In this talk, Li reflects on how change has shaped her understanding of herself. Known to many as a television host, producer, and media entrepreneur, she looks back on the stages of her life not as a smooth path of success, but as a series of decisions that required courage, responsibility, and a willingness to step outside familiar expectations. Her recent work on menopause also opened a new question: when women move into life stages that are often misunderstood or made invisible, how can they speak honestly about their bodies, emotions, and identities?
In Li's view, change is not something to be feared or resisted. It is a way of meeting oneself again — through uncertainty, through physical and emotional tra
title: The Courage to Change and Be Seen Again | JING LI | TEDxThe Bund Women

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Twenty years ago, Lingmei Kong made a decision that few people around her could understand. She left a stable teaching job and chose to become an actress — a path without clear advice, certainty, or a visible future.
What followed was not an immediate breakthrough, but a long process of finding her place through each choice she made. From entering the Central Academy of Drama to building her career on stage and screen, Kong came to understand that a path is not formed only by the opportunities one is given. It is also shaped by the roles one accepts, the uncertainty one endures, and the strength accumulated over time.
At the beginning of her career, she could not always choose the roles she wanted. Instead, she chose to go deeper into the roles available to her, turning limitation into a way of standing firmly on stage. Finding one’s place, in her story, is not a single moment of recognition. It is a long process of choosing, adjusting, and continuing to grow — until the life you have
title: How Do We Turn Uncertainty Into a Place to Stand? | LINGMEI KONG | TEDxThe Bund Women

author: TEDx Talks
description: Using the metaphor of life as a long performance without a script, without retakes, and without the chance to start over, Liu Tianchi reflects on the many roles we take on in life. As an actress, director, and performance educator, she is not only interested in how people act on stage, but also in how we move between different identities in the everyday world. Through her own experience of stepping into the spotlight and returning to the rehearsal room, she examines the double side of being seen: recognition can expand our boundaries, but it can also make us more aware of expectation, responsibility, and pressure. Liu reminds us that the real challenge is not to perform every role perfectly, but to keep the ability to return to ourselves. In her view, the other side of a highlight is not failure or disappearance, but the ordinary life where we continue to sense, adjust, and live as who we truly are. TIANCHI LIU is Associate Professor of Acting at the Central Academy of Drama and one o
title: If Life Is a Long Performance, Are We Still Playing Ourselves?  | TIANCHI LIU | TEDxThe Bund Women

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the moment you think you've understood someone is the moment you've stopped trying? In this talk, James coins and examines the "completion moment," the instant our minds decide we've seen enough of someone and let the label stand as a verdict. He invites us to resist premature certainty about each other, arguing that in an era of algorithmic feeds and AI summaries, choosing inquiry over conclusion is one of the most humane acts left to us. James Mathai is a student at Northeastern University London studying Bioengineering and Biochemistry. He has a strong interest in the intersection of science, innovation, and human potential, particularly in how biological systems and engineering principles can be applied to solve complex real-world problems.

Through his studies, James explores how analytical thinking and scientific understanding can shape new perspectives on growth, resilience, and possibility. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but indepen
title: The Completion Moment  | James Mathai | TEDxNortheasternU London

author: TEDx Talks
description:
“No means no” has become one of the most important principles in conversations about consent. It marks a necessary boundary, especially in a world where women’s voices, refusals, and experiences have too often been ignored or dismissed. But once consent becomes the bottom line, another question emerges: what else is needed for intimacy, freedom, and equality to truly exist?
For philosopher Jing Xie, consent is never only a matter of individual choice. The ability to say “yes” or “no” is shaped by power, social norms, gendered expectations, and the conditions in which people learn to understand their own desires. Refusal can be difficult. Desire can be unclear. Autonomy can be constrained long before a decision is made.
Consent must remain a bottom line, but it cannot be the end of our imagination. A better relationship requires more than the absence of harm; it requires the conditions for people to understand themselves, express their will, and approach one another without fear, contr
title: What Comes After “No Means No”?  | JING XIE | TEDxThe Bund Women

description: In a world driven by trends, how much of what we think is truly our own? This talk explores how fast-moving content can blur the line between independent thought and repetition, and why pausing to question what we see, share, and believe has never been more important. It’s a reflection on choice, awareness, and the quiet power of thinking for yourself. Mansoor AlFalahi is a 17-year-old student with a strong interest in understanding the dynamics of social media and its influence on independent thinking. He focuses on observing patterns within online platforms, particularly how rapidly evolving trends can shape perspectives and affect independent thinking. author: TEDx Talks
description: Using the question “Why is it so hard to take our mothers to the doctor?” as his starting point, Liucenglou examines the hesitation, fear, and communication barriers hidden behind women’s health decisions. Drawing from his experience as a former obstetrician-gynecologist and longtime women’s health educator, he has seen that many physical problems are not only delayed by a lack of medical knowledge, but also by silence, avoidance, and the difficulty of speaking about the body within families. Through real cases from his work, he reminds us that even a small symptom can be a signal that should not be ignored, and that caring for our mothers often begins with learning how to listen, ask, and accompany. Liucenglou argues that family care is not only about taking someone to the hospital, but about rebuilding trust across generations, making women’s health easier to talk about, and helping more people seek help before it is too late. LIUCENGLOU bridges medical expertise and public understa
title: Why Is It So Hard to Take Our Mothers to the Doctor? | MR. LIUCENGLOU | TEDxThe Bund Women

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Many remember Qian Yang for one unforgettable moment: winning Olympic gold with her final shot in Tokyo. Yet for Yang, that moment was only one point in a much longer journey — one shaped by years of repetition, pressure, adjustment, and quiet discipline.
Long before the spotlight of victory, there were ordinary days of training: raising the gun, aiming, firing, and learning to stay with her own heartbeat, breath, and attention. As both a shooting athlete and a graduate student, Yang has moved between two tracks — the precision of competition and the demands of study — while constantly making choices about what matters most at each stage.
Her story is not only about winning, but about learning how to steady oneself through change. Life, for Yang, is not measured only by the moments seen by others. It is built through the quiet days when no one is watching, and through the ability to keep finding one’s rhythm amid pauses, restarts, and uncertainty. This talk was given at a TEDx event u
title: Beyond Olympics Gold Medal: Finding Your Own Rhythm | QIAN YANG | TEDxThe Bund Women

description:
TEDxMarunouchiのオープニング「Discovery of being」は、生きる美しさを再認識するための多感覚アートステージです。

観客は音楽に合わせた「意識的な呼吸」を行い、植物の生体信号と音の振動で水面に描かれる「水の曼荼羅」を鑑賞します。さらに、特殊な電気技術「ドラゴンサウンド」と、般若心経とビートボックスの融合により、観客は思考を手放し深い瞑想状態へと導かれます。目に見えない命の本質や自身の存在感を感じるこの時間は、全ての生命の幸せを祈る言葉とともに幕を閉じます。

The TEDxMarunouchi opening, "Discovery of Being," is a multi-sensory experience. It blends ancient spiritual practices with modern technology to help the audience rediscover the beauty of life.

The performance centers on conscious breathing, visual perception, and resonance. Guided by live music, attendees practice mindful breathing while watching "water mandalas"—unique geometric patterns created by converting plant bio-signals into sound vibrations. Enhanced by "Dragon Sound" technology and Akasaka's fusion of human beatboxing and the Heart Sutra, participants are guided into a deep meditative state. This immersive session allows the audience to feel the unseen essence of life, concluding with a prayer for all living creatures. "ヒューマンビートボク
title: Discovery of Being  | Yogetsu Akasaka 赤坂陽月, Keigo Tanaka 田中圭吾 & Keizo Arai 荒井景三 | TEDxMarunouchi

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Each generation inherits a more degraded world and accepts it as normal: fewer birds, fewer fireflies, fewer fish. When examined, the loss is staggering. In North America alone, we've lost 3 billion birds in a human lifespan. The good news is we know how to bring them back. Take the piping plover, a New England shorebird that fits in the palm of your hand, which recovered from 200 breeding pairs to 1,200 through steady, unglamorous conservation efforts. While there is no shortage of stories of wildlife disappearing, nature is built to recover. And policy is a powerful lever to break the cycle of decline. Through new biodiversity benchmarks, Massachusetts is showcasing what is possible when we act with intention, set real goals, and refuse to quit even without certainty of success.
 Tom O'Shea is Executive Director of the Massachusetts Environmental Trust, a state agency that funds conservation, restoration, and environmental education projects across the Commonwealth. He has spent mor
title: How to restore nature before we forget what we've lost | Tom O'Shea | TEDxBoston

author: TEDx Talks
description: A young Florida black bear walked 500 miles from the edge of Disney to the outskirts of Fort Myers. This journey proved to researchers that a viable wildlife corridor still existed in a state increasingly crowded with development as population booms. When that critical natural pathway was slated for a major highway project, photographer Carlton Ward Jr. took action to protect the land generations of his family had called home. He'd spend the next 15 years building a movement, one frame at a time, photographing panthers, ranches, and wild places to give the corridor a face and a story people could root for. His images of a critically endangered female Florida panther pushing north into the Everglades for the first time in 50 years showed what was at stake through the eyes of an individual. The story was covered internationally, and the community rallied. The Florida Wildlife Corridor Act was passed in 2021 with unanimous bipartisan support (seriously!), and the state has since committe
title: Give people a story to root for instead of a policy to fight over | Carlton Ward Jr. | TEDxBoston

description:
Мы привыкли думать, что будущее можно просчитать: эксперты делают прогнозы, писатели-фантасты придумывают правила для новых технологий, а каждое поколение уверено, что понимает, что ждёт следующее. Но история показывает обратное: мы снова и снова ошибаемся в своих предсказаниях. И всё же продолжаем жить, выбирать, переезжать, начинать заново и строить новое.
Это выступление — личный рассказ о нескольких поколениях одной семьи, удивительных пересечениях с историей робототехники и IT и о том, чему нас может научить опыт людей, которым приходилось действовать без гарантий и готовых ответов. Разговор о времени, человеческой устойчивости и о том, что, возможно, главный навык будущего — не умение его предсказать, а готовность делать следующий шаг, даже когда исход неизвестен.

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Держа в одной руке коробку с карандашами, а другой указывая на карандаши, рассыпанные по красному ковру, физик Светлана Волчак спрашивает: в чём разница? Порядок против беспорядка — и, как оказывается, в этом скрыт секрет самого времени. От обратимой ньютоновской вселенной-часового механизма до энтропии, второго закона термодинамики и неизбежной тепловой смерти вселенной — она объясняет, почему время течёт не просто из прошлого в будущее, а из состояния с меньшей энтропией в состояние с большей, от порядка к беспорядку. Но есть то, что противостоит этому космическому сползанию в хаос, — сама жизнь и наша способность строить, организовывать и создавать. Даже если для начала это просто — собрать рассыпанные карандаши.
—
Holding a box of pencils in one hand and pointing to pencils scattered across the red carpet in the other, physicist Sviatlana Volchak asks: what's the real difference? Order versus disorder — and, it turns out, that's also the secret of time itself. From Newton's revers
title: Куды ідзе час | Sviatlana Volchak | TEDxUlica Mińska

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Это выступление — не только о литературе, но и о праве на существование. Татьяна Замировская рассказывает о том, как однажды услышала от представителей литературного сообщества: «Тебя нет», потому что она писала на русском языке и не соответствовала представлению о том, каким должен быть «настоящий» белорусский писатель. Через личную историю отказа, эмиграции и смены языка она исследует, как формируется культурная идентичность и кто вообще имеет право определять принадлежность человека к литературе и стране.
В то же время это разговор о природе творчества. О том, что рассказы не всегда создаются усилием воли — иногда они приходят сами, когда человек находит язык, в котором может услышать собственный голос. Это выступление о том, как из опыта невидимости и непризнания вырастает свобода быть собой: писать, несмотря на чужие определения, и заново присваивать себе право говорить от своего имени.
//
This talk is not only about literature — it is about the right to exist. Tatyana Zamirovska
title: Как стать беларусским писателем, когда цябе няма | Tatyana Zamirovskaya | TEDxUlica Mińska
